questions.q: What is the burden in this chapter?
questions.a: It is a burden of the Valley of Vision.

questions.q: Where have all the people gone?
questions.a: They have all gone up to the housetops.

questions.q: What is happening in the city and town?
questions.a: The city is noisy and the town full of revelry.

questions.q: Did the dead die by the sword or in battle?
questions.a: No, the dead did not die by the sword or in battle.

questions.q: What happened to their rulers?
questions.a: Their rulers fled away together and were caught and captured together.

questions.q: Why was Isaiah weeping bitterly?
questions.a: He was weeping because of the destruction of the daughter of his people.

questions.q: What kind of day is it in the Valley of Vision?
questions.a: It is a day of trouble and confusion, when the wall is broken down and the people cry out to Yahweh for help.

questions.q: Who is taking up the quiver and shield against them?
questions.a: Elam takes up the quiver and Kir lays the shield bare.

questions.q: What happened in Judah’s choicest valleys?
questions.a: Their valleys became full of chariots.

questions.q: What did God do with the protection of Judah?
questions.a: God removed the protection of Judah.

questions.q: What did the people do when they saw the many breaks in the walls of the city of David?
questions.a: They gathered the water of the lower pool.

questions.q: What did the people do with some of the houses of Jerusalem?
questions.a: They tore down some houses to provide material to fortify the wall.

questions.q: Whom did the people not look to, even though they built a reservoir for water?
questions.a: They did not look to Yahweh, the one who made the pool of water long ago.

questions.q: What did the people do instead of weeping and mourning?
questions.a: The people celebrated and were glad. They were killing cattle and sheep, eating meat and drinking wine.

questions.q: What did Yahweh of Armies call for on that day?
questions.a: He called for weeping and mourning, for shaved heads and the wearing of sackcloth.

questions.q: Will the Lord forgive the people for their response?
questions.a: The Lord will not forgive them even when they die.

questions.q: What did Shebna, the steward, do for himself?
questions.a: Shebna had a tomb hewn for himself in the rock.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would do to Shebna?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would throw Shebna down and remove him from his office and station.

questions.q: Who was to take Shebna’s place of authority?
questions.a: Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah was to take Shebna’s place of authority.

questions.q: What will Yahweh put on Eliakim’s shoulder?
questions.a: Yahweh will put the key of the house of David on his shoulder.

questions.q: What will Eliakim be like, according to Yahweh?
questions.a: He will be like a peg driven into a firm place, and he will bring honor to his father’s house.

questions.q: What will hang on Eliakim, like small vessels on a peg?
questions.a: All the glory of his father’s house, his offspring and descendants, will hang on him.

questions.q: On that day what will happen to the peg driven into a firm place?
questions.a: The peg driven in a firm place will give way, break off and fall and the weight that was on it will be cut off.

commentary.text: The siege and taking of Jerusalem. (Is. 22:1-7) The wicked conduct of its inhabitants. (Is. 22:8-14) The displacing of Shebna, and the promotion of Eliakim, applied to the Messiah. (Is. 22:15-25)

Is. 22:1-7 Why is Jerusalem in such terror? Her slain men are not slain with the sword, but with famine; or, slain with fear, disheartened. Their rulers fled, but were overtaken. The servants of God, who foresee and warn sinners of coming miseries, are affected by the prospect. But all the horrors of a city taken by storm, faintly shadow forth the terrors of the day of wrath.

Is. 22:8-14 The weakness of Judah now appeared more than ever. Now also they discovered their carnal confidence and their carnal security. They looked to the fortifications. They made sure of water for the city. But they were regardless of God in all these preparations. They did not care for his glory in what they did. They did not depend upon him for a blessing on their endeavours. For every creature is to us what God makes it to be; and we must bless him for it, and use it for him. There was great contempt of God's wrath and justice, in contending with them. God's design was to humble them, and bring them to repentance. They walked contrary to this. Actual disbelief of another life after this, is at the bottom of the carnal security and brutish sensuality, which are the sin, the shame, and ruin of so great a part of mankind. God was displeased at this. It is a sin against the remedy, and it is not likely they should ever repent of it. Whether this unbelief works by presumption or despair, it produces the same contempt of God, and is a token that a man will perish wilfully.

Is. 22:15-25 This message to Shebna is a reproof of his pride, vanity, and security; what vanity is all earthly grandeur, which death will so soon end! What will it avail, whether we are laid in a magnificent tomb, or covered with the green sod? Those who, when in power, turn and toss others, will be justly turned and tossed themselves. Eliakim should be put into Shebna's place. Those called to places of trust and power, should seek to God for grace to enable them to do their duty. Eliakim's advancement is described. Our Lord Jesus describes his own power as Mediator, Rev. 3:7, that he has the key of David. His power in the kingdom of heaven, and in ordering all the affairs of that kingdom, is absolute. Rulers should be fathers to those under their government; and the honour men bring unto their families, by their piety and usefulness, is more to be valued than what they derive from them by their names and titles. The glory of this world gives a man no real worth or excellence; it is but hung upon him, and it will soon drop from him. Eliakim was compared to a nail in a sure place; all his family are said to depend upon him. In eastern houses, rows of large spikes were built up in the walls. Upon these the moveables and utensils were hung. Our Lord Jesus is as a nail in a sure place. That soul cannot perish, nor that concern fall to the ground, which is by faith hung upon Christ. He will set before the believer an open door, which no man can shut, and bring both body and soul to eternal glory. But those who neglect so great salvation will find, that when he shutteth none can open, whether it be shutting out from heaven, or shutting up in hell for ever.
